Purchase to receipt

Buy materials on a purchase order, receive them into a warehouse, and check that on-hand rose by what you received.

FieldValueStep

Before you start

  • A buy-from business partner, materials you can buy, and a warehouse to receive them into. To see where an item's stock is first, follow Check an item's inventory.
  • The materials exist as items you can buy, and the warehouse you're buying into exists. Configure the purchased group and Create the three items make both.

Procedure

1Read the baseline

Result
Each material's on-hand at the receiving warehouse is written down.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes yet. A confirmed receipt only tells you a document changed status. The proof that stock arrived is the on-hand figure at the receiving warehouse going up, and that needs the figure from before. A new item isn't always at zero.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Open Inventory 360One row for each item
1.2Type the first material in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterExampleItem BAM-ROD, then BAM-SLEEVE — test items that Create test items makesThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.3Tick the item's own row and click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory opens, one row per warehouseWrite downmaterial 1receiving warehousematerial 1 on-hand before
1.4Close that tab, untick the row, and do the same for the second materialWrite downmaterial 2material 2 on-hand before

2Create the purchase order

Result
The purchase order is saved for your buy-from business partner, with status Created.
Screen
Procurement➔Orders➔Order Intake Workbench (tdpur4601m200)

Why LN works this way. The buy-from business partner fills in most of the header: the order type, the purchase office and the buyer come from the partner's record. The partner has to exist already; this guide picks one and doesn't create one.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Purchase Order Intake WorkbenchThe workbench, with a Purchase Orders tab below
2.2On the Purchase Orders tab, click NewPurchase Order opens, empty, with Status Created
2.3Enter the buy-from Business Partner and press TabIts name and address fill in, and the ship-from with them
2.4Check the Order Type LN fills inExampleOrder Type IPO — Inventory Purchase Order, which LN fills inThe partner's default order type
2.5Check the Purchase Office LN fills inThe partner's purchase office. If LN says Purchase offices for business partner and user differ., you can leave it
2.6Click SaveOrder shows the new numberWrite downpurchase order number
Create the purchase order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The order type isn't IPONothing, if it's the type your partner uses. IPO is what the example used
The partner's name doesn't fill inThe partner may not exist as a buy-from business partner. Check the code, or ask whoever maintains business partners

3Book the lines

Result
Each material is a line of the order, in its quantity, to the receiving warehouse.

Why LN works this way. Each line names an item, a quantity and a warehouse. The warehouse on the line decides where the goods are received, so a line to the wrong warehouse puts the stock somewhere you didn't mean.

StepActionYou should see
3.1On the Order Lines tab under the header, click NewA new line, with Line 10 and the site filled in
3.2Enter the first material as Item and press TabExampleItem BAM-ROD, then BAM-SLEEVEIts description fills in, and Ordered Quantity reads 1
3.3Enter its Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 2 for BAM-ROD and 1 for BAM-SLEEVE, one pair's bill of materialWrite downmaterial 1 quantity ordered
3.4Click New againA second line, 20
3.5Enter the second material as Item and press TabExampleItem BAM-ROD, then BAM-SLEEVEIts description fills in
3.6Enter its Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 2 for BAM-ROD and 1 for BAM-SLEEVE, one pair's bill of materialWrite downmaterial 2 quantity ordered
3.7Click SaveBoth lines are listed
3.8Check Warehouse on each lineLN fills in the item's default warehouse. It should be the receiving warehouse; if it isn't, change it and save

4Approve the purchase order

Result
The purchase order reads In Process, and a warehousing order with its number is listed.

Why LN works this way. Only an approved order goes to Warehousing. Approving prints the purchase order, and in the example it also released the order to Warehousing at once, so a warehousing order with the same number appeared without a separate release. That warehousing order is what you receive against.

StepActionYou should see
4.1On the purchase order's toolbar, click ApproveThe purchase order prints in a tab of its own, sometimes with an annex
4.2Close the print tabs and go back to the purchase orderStatus = In Process
4.3Open Warehousing Orders
4.4Type the purchase order number in the filter box above the Order column and press EnterOne row: Order Origin Purchase, Receipt, Open, Order Type PUI
Approve the purchase order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Approve is greyed outThe order may have no lines yet, or they aren't saved. Go back to Book the lines
No warehousing order after approvingThe lines may not be released yet. Open the purchase order's Release to Warehousing tab: a line still listed there is waiting, and the workbench's Release to Warehousing releases it

5Receive against the order

Result
Warehouse Receipt is open with a line for each purchase order line.
Screen
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders (whinh2100m000)

Why LN works this way. You don't create this order. Approving the purchase order made it, with the same number, and its inbound lines are the purchase order lines waiting to be received. Receiving them opens a receipt with the lines already on it.

StepActionYou should see
5.1On the warehousing order's row, click Drill InWarehousing Order opens, with Inbound Lines below
5.2Check Order Type and the two warehousesOrder Type PUI, ship-from your business partner, ship-to the receiving warehouse
5.3On the Inbound Lines tab, tick every lineOne inbound line for each purchase order line, each Open
5.4On the Inbound Lines toolbar, choose Actions➔Receive…Warehouse Receipt (whinh3512m000) opens
Receive against the order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The Actions menu has no Receive…You may be on the screen's own toolbar. Use the one above the Inbound Lines
The ship-to isn't the receiving warehouseA purchase order line went to another warehouse. Check Warehouse at step 3.8

6Confirm the receipt

Result
The receipt reads Confirmed, with All Lines Final and All Lines Complete set and Errors Logged clear.

Why LN works this way. LN builds the receipt lines from the inbound lines you ticked, each with its full quantity received. Confirming the receipt is what puts the goods into the warehouse. The flags in Status sum up the lines, so read them before you leave.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Read the Receipt number and each line's Received QuantityWrite downreceipt number. Each line has its ordered quantity received
6.2Enter the supplier's Packing Slip on each line and click SaveEach line shows its packing slip
6.3Click Confirm Receipt on the toolbarStatus = Confirmed, and each line's Confirmed is ticked
6.4Check All Lines Final and All Lines CompleteBoth are set
6.5Check Errors LoggedIt's clear. If it's set, open the Message Log tab below and read the messages
Confirm the receipt: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
A message about missing stock point detailsThe warehouse may be missing a setting the receipt needs. Read it on the Message Log tab, and ask whoever set up the warehouse
The packing slip number must be entered on receipt lineA line has no Packing Slip. Choose OK, enter it on each line, save, and confirm again
Confirmed is clear but nothing looks wrongThe receipt may have no lines. Go back to step 5.3 and tick the inbound lines

7Verify the inventory increase

Result
Each material's on-hand at the receiving warehouse rose by its quantity received, once anything else that moved the item is allowed for.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing new. A confirmed receipt is a status. The proof is the on-hand figure at the receiving warehouse going up by what you received.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Read the first material's on-hand at the receiving warehouse, in the same view as step 1.3Write downmaterial 1 on-hand afterup by its quantity ordered
7.2Do the same for the second materialWrite downmaterial 2 on-hand afterup by its quantity ordered
Verify the inventory increase: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
On-hand didn't go upThe receipt may not be confirmed. Check step 6.3
It went up by a different amountSomething else may have moved the item in between. Look for other movements of the item before trusting the result

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Purchase with inspectionAn inspection activity sits between receipt and put-away. Warehouse Inspections (whinh3122m000) runs against the receipt. This adds a task and would earn its own process.
Direct-delivery purchaseGoods ship from the supplier to a customer without entering your warehouse. That removes receiving, confirming and the inventory check entirely, so it is a different process, not a variant of this one
Booking opening stock instead of buyingThe adjustment route the notes of Stock the components describe — a cycle counting/adjustment order. Faster, but it bypasses purchase defaults and leaves no purchase price history. Its entry session was never captured
